instruction: Use VLC and GIMP to create an animated GIF named src_clip.gif from about 5 seconds of the desktop video src.mp4.

metadata.explanation: This task converts approximately 5 seconds of video into an animated GIF using VLC and GIMP. The evaluator checks: (1) the GIF is animated (score 0.4), (2) has a reasonable frame count between 45-175 frames (score 0.3), and (3) has a duration between 3-7 seconds (score 0.3). A 5-second clip at typical frame rates (10-25 fps) would yield 50-125 frames. The duration is calculated from GIF frame delays. Score breakdown: is_animated=0.4, frame_count_in_range=0.3, duration_in_range=0.3.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all requirements - file exists, GIF is animated, duration is approximately 5 seconds (3-7s range)
Correct getter logic: Properly extracts GIF state using PIL, counts frames, and calculates total duration from frame delays
Correct metric logic: Properly compares animation flag, frame count range (45-175), and duration range (3.0-7.0 seconds)
Correct expected values: is_animated=true, duration 3-7s for 'approximately 5 seconds', frame count 45-175 for 5s at 10-35 fps
Proper parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('is_animated') directly for type='rule' (not expected.get('rules'))
No state timing issues: Reads saved GIF file directly, no UI state dependency, no postconfig needed
Good edge case handling: Returns proper fallback values for missing files or corrupted GIFs
